# 1 Samuel Chapter 24 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 164v–165r | **Source Image:** 1SA_024_page_001.jpg, 1SA_024_page_002.jpg

---

**1** After Saul returned from fighting the Philistines, he was told, "David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."

**2** So Saul took three thousand of Israel's best soldiers and went to search for David and his men near the Crags of the Wild Goats.

**3** He came to some sheepfolds along the road where there was a cave. Saul went inside to relieve himself — not knowing that David and his men were hiding deep in the back of that very cave.

**4** David's men whispered, "This is the day the LORD told you about — 'I will hand your enemy over to you to do with as you wish.'" David crept forward and cut off a corner of Saul's robe without being noticed.

**5** But immediately his conscience stung him for what he had done.

**6** He told his men, "The LORD forbid that I should do anything to my master. He is the LORD's anointed — I will not raise my hand against him."

**7** With these words David held his men back and would not let them attack Saul. Saul got up, left the cave, and went on his way.

**8** Then David came out of the cave and called after him, "My lord the king!" Saul turned around, and David bowed facedown to the ground.

**9** David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to people who say I'm trying to harm you?

**10** Today you can see with your own eyes that the LORD put you in my power in that cave. I was urged to kill you, but I spared you. I said, 'I will not raise my hand against my master — he is the LORD's anointed.'

**11** Look, my father — look at this piece of your robe in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe but did not kill you. Doesn't this prove there is no treachery or rebellion in me? I have not wronged you, yet you are hunting me down to take my life.

**12** May the LORD judge between us. May the LORD vindicate me against you — but my hand will never touch you.

**13** As the old proverb says, 'From wicked people comes wickedness' — but my hand will never touch you.

**14** Who is the king of Israel chasing? A dead dog? A single flea?

**15** May the LORD be the judge. May He decide between us, take up my cause, and deliver me from your hand."

**16** When David finished speaking, Saul said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" And Saul broke down and wept.

**17** "You are a better man than I am," he said. "You have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with evil.

**18** Today you have shown how well you have treated me — the LORD delivered me into your hands and you did not kill me.

**19** What man, finding his enemy, lets him walk away unharmed? May the LORD reward you for what you have done for me today.

**20** I know now that you will certainly be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be secure in your hands.

**21** Now swear to me by the LORD that you will not wipe out my descendants and that you will not erase my family name."

**22** David gave Saul his oath. Then Saul went home, and David and his men returned to the stronghold.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **24:3 — the cave**: The scene is almost comedic in its setup — the king of Israel, with three thousand soldiers, walks alone into the one cave where his fugitive rival is hiding. The narrator wants you to see the absurdity and the providence simultaneously.

2. **24:5 — "his conscience stung him"**: David's heart "struck him" for cutting Saul's robe. Not for an act of violence — for a symbolic violation. Even the garment of the LORD's anointed is sacred. This extraordinary moral sensitivity is what makes David David.

3. **24:14 — "a dead dog, a single flea"**: David's self-deprecation is strategic but also genuine. He is asking: why would a king mobilize an army to hunt a nobody? The absurdity of Saul's obsession is the point.

4. **24:16-21 — Saul's tears**: This is Saul at his most lucid and most tragic. He sees the truth clearly — David is righteous, David will be king — and he cannot change course. He weeps because he knows. His request to protect his descendants acknowledges that David's dynasty will replace his own.

— PNEUMA
